Question: Does the platform maintain a centralised catalogue of approved models? Describe the registry.
Response: Yes. Foundry Control Plane provides a centralised model registry with the full Foundry model catalog (1900+ models). Administrators control which models are available per project. APIM AI Gateway adds a governance layer: model routing policies define which models are accessible, with load balancing, failover, token limits, and cost tracking per model. The combination provides: catalogue of approved models (Foundry), governed access and usage policies (APIM), and cost/usage visibility (APIM metrics + OTEL telemetry). Models are selectable per skill — cheap models for triage tasks, frontier models for high-value reasoning — all governed centrally.
Key Technologies: Foundry model catalog, APIM AI Gateway model routing, Foundry Control Plane
POC Demo: POC1: Show model registry in Foundry with APIM governance policies controlling access.

Question: Can you define and enforce metadata per model: training set provenance, data cutoff dates, licensing (FOSS vs proprietary), parameter counts?
Response: Foundry model catalog includes metadata per model: provider, version, licensing terms, parameter counts, capabilities, and supported regions. APIM AI Gateway policies can enforce constraints based on model metadata — e.g. restrict proprietary models to production environments only, or enforce region constraints (EU-only models for GDPR workflows). Model versioning in Foundry prevents silent updates: specific model versions are pinned in skill configurations and APIM routing policies. Training set provenance and data cutoff dates are available where model providers publish them, surfaced in the Foundry catalog.
Key Technologies: Foundry model catalog metadata, APIM policy enforcement

Question: Does the registry support model versioning to prevent silent updates from breaking agent behaviour?
Response: Yes. Model versions are pinned at two levels. (1) Skill-level: each SKILL.md can specify the model version it requires. (2) APIM-level: model routing policies reference specific model deployment versions. Model updates require explicit promotion through the CI/CD pipeline — a new model version is deployed as a separate endpoint, tested via Foundry Evaluators, and promoted only after passing quality gates. APIM supports blue-green model deployments: route a percentage of traffic to the new model version, compare quality metrics, and switch fully only after validation. Silent updates from model providers are prevented because we deploy specific model versions to Azure OpenAI endpoints, not floating latest versions.
Key Technologies: Foundry model deployments, APIM blue-green routing, skill model pinning

Question: Can administrators restrict model access by user group, agent sensitivity, or deployment environment? How do you prevent shadow AI (developers connecting to unapproved endpoints)?
Response: APIM AI Gateway is the single entry point for all model calls. No agent can bypass APIM to reach a model endpoint directly — network-level enforcement ensures all traffic routes through the gateway. Administrators restrict access by: (1) Agent identity — Entra RBAC scopes which models each Hosted Agent can access. (2) Environment — separate APIM configurations for dev/staging/production with different model allowlists. (3) Sensitivity — APIM policies can restrict frontier models to high-sensitivity workflows only. Shadow AI prevention: APIM is the only route to model endpoints. Direct endpoint access is blocked at the network level via Azure Private Endpoints and NSGs. All model calls are logged and auditable. Foundry Control Plane surfaces unauthorised access attempts.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway (single entry point), Entra RBAC, Azure Private Endpoints, Foundry Control Plane

Question: Does the platform maintain a centralised catalogue of approved agents, including use-cases and risk levels?
Response: Yes. Two complementary registries. (1) Foundry Control Plane: provides a centralised agent inventory across all platforms (Foundry-native, custom, external) with lifecycle operations, risk classification, and compliance posture. (2) Azure API Center: registers skills with metadata — capabilities, allowed tools, risk level, lifecycle stage (Design/Preview/Production/Deprecated), version history. Since our architecture uses skills as the unit of capability rather than separate agents, the skill registry in API Center IS the functional agent registry — each skill represents a specialised capability (screening, sourcing, compliance, offer generation) with its own metadata and governance. Agent 365 adds another layer: agent registration in the M365 admin center with Entra Agent ID, Purview, and Defender integration.
Key Technologies: Foundry Control Plane, Azure API Center, Agent 365
POC Demo: POC1: Show skill registry in API Center with lifecycle states and risk levels.

Question: Can you define and enforce metadata per agent: capabilities, knowledge sources, tools employed, risk level?
Response: Yes. Each skill registered in Azure API Center carries enforced metadata: declared capabilities (what the skill does), allowed tools (which MCP servers it can invoke — enforced by GHCP SDK hooks), knowledge sources (which data stores it can access), risk level (determines HITL requirements and autonomy thresholds), lifecycle stage, and version. APIM policies enforce tool access per skill — a skill cannot invoke an MCP tool it has not declared. GHCP SDK session hooks enforce the tool allowlist at runtime: if a skill attempts to call an undeclared tool, the hook blocks it and logs the violation. Agent 365 extends this with Purview-enforced data classification and Defender threat detection per agent identity.
Key Technologies: Azure API Center skill metadata, GHCP SDK hooks (tool allowlisting), APIM policy enforcement, Agent 365

Question: Does the registry support agent versioning to support lifecycle management (dev to prod)?
Response: Yes. Azure API Center provides full lifecycle management for skills: Design -> Preview -> Production -> Deprecated. Each version is immutable once promoted. Version history is maintained with author, timestamp, and change description. Promotion between stages requires approval gates configured in the CI/CD pipeline. Skills are Git-synced — API Center integrates with GitHub Actions workflows for syncing SKILL.md files from repositories, so version control is native to the development workflow. Rollback is supported by promoting a previous version. Concurrent versions can run in different environments (v2 in staging, v1 in production) with environment-specific APIM routing.
Key Technologies: Azure API Center lifecycle management, Git sync, CI/CD approval gates

Question: Can administrators restrict agent access by user group, sensitivity, or deployment environment?
Response: Yes. Access restriction operates at multiple levels. (1) Entra RBAC: Hosted Agent containers have scoped Entra Agent IDs — the Hiring Agent and Finance Agent have separate identities with different tool access. (2) API Center lifecycle: skills in Design/Preview stages are not accessible in production environments. (3) APIM policies: per-environment, per-agent routing and access control. (4) Agent 365: administrators manage agent visibility and access in the M365 admin center — restrict which users can interact with which agents. (5) Control Plane UI: role-based views filter which workflows and capabilities are visible to each operator role. Conditional Access policies on agent identities enforce environment and compliance constraints.
Key Technologies: Entra Agent ID + RBAC, API Center lifecycle gates, APIM per-environment policies, Agent 365 admin
POC Demo: POC2: Show HR BP seeing only hiring workflows, Finance BP seeing only budget gates in Control Plane.

Question: Can the platform continually monitor third-party models for bias, drift, and robustness; generating alerts when test conditions fail?
Response: Yes. Foundry Evaluators run continuous evaluation on production traffic measuring: task adherence (is the agent doing what it should), tool call accuracy, safety, groundedness, and sensitive data exposure. Custom evaluators can be configured for bias detection and domain-specific quality metrics. APIM AI Gateway tracks per-model metrics: latency, error rates, token usage, cost — anomalies trigger alerts. The Fleet Manager agent consumes telemetry from Foundry Evaluators and APIM metrics, reasoning about fleet-wide quality trends. When evaluation scores drift below thresholds, the Fleet Manager surfaces alerts on the Control Plane with recommended actions (revert model version, adjust routing, increase HITL oversight). Azure Monitor and Application Insights provide the alerting infrastructure.
Key Technologies: Foundry Evaluators, APIM AI Gateway metrics, Fleet Manager agent, Azure Monitor
POC Demo: POC2: Show Foundry Evaluator running on CV screening output — detecting quality drift and alerting on Control Plane.

Question: How do you establish, authenticate, and manage the lifecycle of an agent's identity, including permissions, roles, and access controls?
Response: Entra Agent ID (part of Agent 365) establishes agents as first-class identities in Microsoft Entra ID. Each Hosted Agent container has a dedicated Entra Agent ID (e.g. hiring-agent@wpp, finance-agent@wpp, fleet-manager@wpp). The identity is domain-scoped: the Hiring Agent's identity grants access to Greenhouse, LinkedIn, Workday (hiring), Graph, and ACS — not finance systems. Lifecycle management: Agent 365 manages from creation to retirement with responsible person oversight throughout. Permissions: Azure RBAC scopes tool access per agent identity. OBO flows: when a human triggers an action, the agentic loop can act on-behalf-of that human — audit trail attributes the decision to them, downstream access uses their delegated permissions. For autonomous phases, the loop uses the Hosted Agent's app-only identity. Conditional Access policies apply to agent identities just as they do to human identities.
Key Technologies: Entra Agent ID, Agent 365 lifecycle management, Azure RBAC, OBO flows
POC Demo: POC2: Show distinct agent identities in Entra with scoped permissions — Hiring Agent accessing only HR systems.

Question: How does the platform integrate with enterprise identity systems (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, Okta, Entra ID)?
Response: Full integration with WPP's identity landscape. Okta: primary IdP, federated via Entra External ID for SAML-bridged access to business systems (Workday, Greenhouse). Entra ID: native identity platform for all agent and human identities. OAuth 2.0 flows: Authorization Code (LinkedIn), Client Credentials (service-to-service), SAML-bridged (Workday via Okta), PKCE (web portal), Device Flow, OBO (Graph API calls on behalf of human). All auth complexity is abstracted at the platform level — agent developers do not manage tokens. APIM AI Gateway handles auth injection for all MCP tool calls. Automatic token refresh across all grant types without agent awareness. Azure Key Vault stores credentials with automated rotation.
Key Technologies: Entra ID, Entra External ID (Okta federation), APIM auth injection, Azure Key Vault
POC Demo: POC1: Show SAML-bridged Workday access via Okta federation — agent authenticates seamlessly through APIM.

Question: How does the platform address auditability, non-repudiation, and secure credential management for agents?
Response: Auditability: every action is logged — OTEL spans capture tool calls with workflow context (who, what, when, why), APIM logs all model and tool interactions, Foundry Tracing provides full execution traces. All logs flow to Azure Log Analytics with 7-12 year retention (immutability enforced via Azure Storage export with immutability policies). Non-repudiation: Entra Agent ID ties every action to a specific agent identity. OBO flows attribute human-triggered actions to the human's identity. The action ledger in the workflow state store maintains an append-only record of all actions (revocable and non-revocable) with the identity that authorised each. Secure credential management: Azure Key Vault stores all secrets (API keys, certificates, connection strings). APIM injects credentials into MCP tool calls at runtime — agent code never sees raw credentials. Automated credential rotation via Key Vault policies without agent downtime. Microsoft Sentinel provides security incident investigation across all audit data.
Key Technologies: OTEL tracing, Azure Log Analytics (immutable), Entra Agent ID, Azure Key Vault, Microsoft Sentinel
POC Demo: POC1: Show full audit trail for an invoice approval — trace from human decision through agent execution to system write-back.

Question: Describe supported tool-use patterns (MCP, REST/OpenAPI, etc.), tool registry, and tool-level access control.
Response: Tool-use patterns: (1) MCP — primary pattern. Enterprise systems exposed as MCP servers with typed tool definitions. GHCP SDK natively discovers and invokes MCP tools. (2) REST-to-MCP gateway — APIM auto-generates MCP tool definitions from OpenAPI specs, bridging REST APIs into the MCP ecosystem at build-time. (3) REST/OpenAPI — direct invocation via GHCP SDK tool definitions for systems that don't warrant a full MCP server. Tool registry: APIM AI Gateway maintains the centralised tool catalog with metadata (description, auth requirements, rate limits, SLA, owning team, supported environments). Skills declare which tools they use. Agents discover available tools through APIM. Tool-level access control: APIM policies enforce per-agent, per-environment, per-tool access. GHCP SDK session hooks enforce tool allowlists per skill. Rate limiting per agent per tool. Content safety filtering on tool inputs/outputs.
Key Technologies: MCP servers, APIM REST-to-MCP gateway, APIM tool catalog, GHCP SDK hooks
POC Demo: POC1: Show APIM tool catalog with registered MCP servers. Show hook blocking an undeclared tool call.

Question: Describe your platform's observability and management capabilities: traces, metrics, logs, dashboards.
Response: Three-layer observability. (1) Foundry Tracing (OTEL): every agentic loop emits OpenTelemetry spans via TracerProvider — model calls, tool calls, tokens, latency, cost. Spans carry workflow ID, phase, jurisdiction, model, token count. Foundry Agent Monitoring Dashboard provides out-of-box visibility. (2) APIM AI Gateway metrics: token usage, latency, errors per model/tool/agent. Central cost tracking across all AI assets. (3) Fleet Manager assessment: event-driven reasoning over telemetry producing fleet health assessment, SLA risk analysis, anomaly detection, and exception prioritisation. This is the default Control Plane view — intelligent, not raw telemetry. Dashboards: Foundry Control Plane for platform-level monitoring. Custom Control Plane UI for operator experience (fleet dashboard, exception queue, situational awareness drill-down). Application Insights for deep technical investigation. Cost attribution per workflow, phase, model, and consumer visible across all dashboards.
Key Technologies: Foundry Tracing (OTEL), APIM metrics, Fleet Manager agent, Application Insights, Custom Control Plane UI
POC Demo: POC1: Show end-to-end OTEL trace for an invoice workflow — from intake through payment with cost attribution per phase.

Question: What mechanisms exist to intercept and intervene in an agent's execution loop in real-time?
Response: Three intervention mechanisms. (1) GHCP SDK session hooks (onPreToolUse, onPostToolUse): intercept every tool call inside the agentic loop. Non-revocable actions are blocked and routed to the human's PA for approval. Hooks can modify, block, or redirect tool calls based on runtime policy. (2) Foundry Guardrails: intercept at four points (input, output, tool-call, tool-response). PII detection blocks sensitive data. Task Adherence detects policy drift from the agent's system message. Content safety policies block inappropriate content. (3) APIM AI Gateway: intercept model and tool calls at the network level — content filtering, token limits, rate limiting. For human intervention: operators can terminate a running agentic loop from the Control Plane (cancel the GHCP SDK session via API), and pause workflows at phase boundaries (Durable Functions suspends the orchestration at zero compute). Agentic loop phases are short-lived — the meaningful intervention point is between phases, not mid-reasoning. Operators can inspect current state, modify parameters, and resume or terminate from the Control Plane. The Fleet Manager surfaces workflows needing attention before the operator needs to look for them.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK hooks, Foundry Guardrails, APIM AI Gateway, Control Plane UI, Durable Functions suspend/resume
POC Demo: POC1: Demonstrate hook intercepting a payment execution, routing to Finance BP for approval, and deterministic execution after approval.

Question: Does the platform support enforcing policy-as-code to prevent excessive agency before an action completes?
Response: Yes. Policy enforcement operates through code-committed artefacts at every layer. (1) APIM policies: version-controlled via APIOps CI/CD. Define model routing rules, token limits, content safety, rate limiting. Changes require PR review with author/timestamp/rationale. (2) GHCP SDK hooks: Python functions that enforce rules inside the agentic loop — tool allowlisting, non-revocable action interception, audit logging. Hooks are committed to Git alongside skills. (3) Foundry Guardrails configuration: per-agent guardrail policies configured in Foundry, controlling intervention points and enforcement actions. (4) Autonomy thresholds: stored in the workflow configuration store, version-controlled, audit-trailed with operator identity for every change. (5) Jurisdiction-specific skills: compliance rules declared in SKILL.md files per jurisdiction (USA, Germany, etc.), loaded automatically based on workflow context. All policy artefacts are Git-committed, PR-reviewable, and audit-trailed.
Key Technologies: APIOps CI/CD, GHCP SDK hooks, Foundry Guardrails, jurisdiction skills, Git version control
POC Demo: POC2: Show autonomy threshold change on Control Plane — audit trail captures who changed it, when, and why.

Question: Can we audit the specific model versions, system prompts, and tool definitions actively running in a given agent instance?
Response: Yes. Full inspectability at every level. (1) Model versions: OTEL spans record the exact model version used for every inference call. APIM logs the model endpoint and version per request. (2) System prompts: skills (SKILL.md files) are the system prompts — they are Git-versioned, registered in API Center with version history. The exact skill version active in a workflow phase is recorded in the workflow state. (3) Tool definitions: the MCP tools available to each agentic loop are determined by the skill's declared tool allowlist, registered in APIM. OTEL spans record every tool call with parameters and results. All inspectable from: Foundry Control Plane (agent inventory, model deployments), Application Insights (KQL queries on OTEL traces), Custom Control Plane UI (situational awareness drill-down showing skills, models, and tools for any workflow phase).
Key Technologies: OTEL tracing, Azure API Center version history, APIM logs, Application Insights KQL
POC Demo: POC1: Drill into a specific invoice workflow — show which skill version, model version, and tool definitions were active at each phase.

Question: How does the platform log and visualise the full chain-of-thought and execution path? Can we trace an action back to the reasoning step and tool call that triggered it?
Response: Full traceability through OTEL instrumentation. Every agentic loop emits spans that capture: the skill loaded, the model called (with version), the reasoning produced, each tool call (with parameters and results), the decision made, and the action taken. Spans are correlated by workflow ID and phase, creating a complete execution graph. Visualisation: Foundry Tracing provides the raw trace view with reasoning steps and tool calls. Application Insights supports KQL queries for cross-workflow trace analysis. The Custom Control Plane UI provides situational awareness: click any workflow -> see the full execution path with what agents did, why the workflow stopped, what the agent recommends, and what the options are. Trace-to-action: every entry in the action ledger (e.g. 'payment submitted to D365') links back to the OTEL span that produced it, including the reasoning chain and tool call that triggered it. This is queryable from both Foundry and the Control Plane UI.
Key Technologies: Foundry Tracing (OTEL spans), Application Insights, Custom Control Plane UI, action ledger
POC Demo: POC1: Trace a payment action back through the full reasoning chain — show the model reasoning, validation tool calls, and approval that led to it.
